items.stem: The curve y = (x − 3)² + 5 has a minimum point. What are its coordinates?
items.markingKey: Minimum where (x − 3)² = 0, i.e. x = 3, y = 5.

items.stem: Explain why the least value of (x − p)² + q is q, and state the value of x at which it occurs.
items.answer: A square is never negative, so (x − p)² ≥ 0 and the expression is at least q; it equals q only when x = p.
items.markingKey: B1 (x − p)² ≥ 0; B1 least value q when x = p [2]

items.stem: Explain how completing the square on ax² + bx + c shows whether the graph has a maximum or a minimum point.
items.answer: Writing it as a(x + p)² + q, the squared term is ≥ 0. If a > 0 the expression is least (minimum q) when x = −p; if a < 0 it is greatest (maximum q).
items.markingKey: B1 sign of a decides min/max; B1 vertex (−p, q) from the completed square [2]

items.stem: Express x² − 8x + 25 in the form (x + a)² + b, and hence state the coordinates of the vertex of y = x² − 8x + 25.
items.markingKey: B1 a = −4; B1 b = 9; B1 vertex (4, 9)

items.stem: Express x² + 5x + 1 in the form (x + a)² + b, where a and b are constants, and state the least value of the expression.
items.markingKey: B1 a = 5/2; B1 b = −21/4; B1 least value −21/4 when x = −5/2

items.stem: Express 2x² + 16x + 32 in the form a(x + b)² + c. Hence state the coordinates of the minimum point of y = 2x² + 16x + 32.
The function f is defined by f(x) = x² − 4x for x ∈ ℝ. (a) Solve the equation f(x) = 12. (b) Find the set of values of t for which the equation f(x) = t has no real roots.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 (x − 2)² = 16; M1 x − 2 = ±4; A1 x = −2, 6 [3] (b) B1 t < −4 (graph never reaches below the vertex) [1]

items.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = 3x² + 6x + 13 for x ∈ ℝ. (a) Express f(x) in the form a(x + b)² + c. (b) Write down the coordinates of the vertex of the graph of y = f(x). (c) State the range of f. (d) Find the set of values of t for which the equation f(x) = t has no real roots.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 b = 1; B1 c = 10 [2] (b) B1 FT (−1, 10) [1] (c) B1 f(x) ≥ 10 [1] (d) B1 t < 10 (graph never reaches below the vertex) [1]

items.stem: What is the least value of (x + 4)² − 7 as x varies?
items.markingKey: (x + 4)² ≥ 0, so the least value is 0 − 7 = −7, when x = −4.

items.stem: Which expression is equal to x² − 16x + 11?
items.markingKey: Halve the coefficient of x: (x − 8)² = x² − 16x + 64, so subtract 64: (x − 8)² − 53.

items.stem: Explain why the quadratic x² + 6x + 10 is positive for all real values of x.
items.answer: x² + 6x + 10 = (x + 3)² + 1, and (x + 3)² ≥ 0, so the expression is at least 1 > 0.
items.markingKey: B1 (x + 3)² + 1; B1 square ≥ 0 so ≥ 1 > 0 [2]

items.stem: By completing the square, show that x² + 8x + 26 > 0 for all real values of x.
items.markingKey: M1 completes the square (x + 4)² + 10; A1 states square ≥ 0 so expression ≥ 10 > 0

items.stem: The curve y = x² + bx + c has its minimum point at (−8, 2). Find the values of b and c.
items.markingKey: M1 y = (x + 8)² + 2; M1 expands; A1 b = 16, c = 66

items.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = x² − 2x + 4 for x ∈ ℝ. By completing the square, find the range of f.
items.markingKey: M1 f(x) = (x − 1)² + 3; A1 least value 3; B1 range f(x) ≥ 3

items.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = x² + 12x + 16 for x ∈ ℝ. (a) Express f(x) in the form (x + b)² + c. (b) State the range of f. (c) Find the set of values of t for which the equation f(x) = t has no real roots.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 b = 6; B1 c = −20 [2] (b) B1 f(x) ≥ −20 [1] (c) B1 t < −20 (graph never reaches below the vertex) [1]

items.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = x² − 4x − 5 for x ∈ ℝ. (a) Solve the equation f(x) = 16. (b) Describe fully the single transformation that maps the graph of y = x² onto the graph of y = f(x).
items.answer: (a) x = −3 or x = 7 (b) Translation by vector (2, −9)
items.markingKey: (a) M1 (x − 2)² = 25; M1 x − 2 = ±5; A1 x = −3, 7 [3] (b) B1 translation; B1 vector (2, −9) [2]

items.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = 2x² − 12x + 11 for x ∈ ℝ. (a) Write down the coordinates of the vertex of the graph of y = f(x). (b) State the range of f. (c) Solve the equation f(x) = −5. (d) Find the set of values of t for which the equation f(x) = t has no real roots.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 FT (3, −7) [1] (b) B1 f(x) ≥ −7 [1] (c) M1 2(x − 3)² = 2; M1 x − 3 = ±1; A1 x = 2, 4 [3] (d) B1 t < −7 (graph never reaches below the vertex) [1]

items.stem: For the equation ax² + bx + c = 0, which condition gives two equal (repeated) real roots?
items.markingKey: Equal roots when the discriminant is zero.

items.stem: Explain why the equation ax² + bx + c = 0 must have two distinct real roots when a and c have opposite signs.
items.answer: If ac < 0 then −4ac > 0, so b² − 4ac > b² ≥ 0 and the discriminant is positive.
items.markingKey: B1 −4ac > 0; B1 b² ≥ 0 so discriminant > 0 [2]

items.stem: Explain how the discriminant of the quadratic obtained by eliminating y tells you whether a line meets a curve at two points, touches it, or does not meet it.
items.answer: Discriminant > 0: two points of intersection; = 0: one repeated point, so the line is a tangent; < 0: no real solutions so no intersection.
items.markingKey: B1 > 0 two points and < 0 no points; B1 = 0 tangent [2]

items.stem: Find the values of k for which the equation 9x² + kx + 9 = 0 has two equal real roots.
The equation kx² − 18x − 3 = 0, where k ≠ 0, has two equal real roots. Find the value of k and the repeated root.
The line y = −5x + k is a tangent to the curve y = x² − 11x + 2. Find the value of k and the coordinates of the point of contact.
items.markingKey: M1 forms x² − 6x + 2 − k = 0; M1 discriminant = 0; A1 k = −7; M1 x = 3; A1 (3, −22)

items.stem: A curve has equation y = x² − 2x + 11 and a line has equation y = 4x + k, where k is a constant. (a) Show that the x-coordinates of any points of intersection satisfy x² − 6x + 11 − k = 0. (b) Find the coordinates of the point of contact when the line is a tangent to the curve. (c) State the number of points of intersection when k = −1.
items.answer: (a) Shown (b) (3, 14) (c) 0 (the line does not meet the curve)
items.markingKey: (a) B1 equates x² − 2x + 11 = 4x + k and rearranges [1] (b) M1 x = 3; A1 (3, 14) [2] (c) B1 0 (discriminant negative since k < 2) [1]

items.stem: A curve has equation y = x² + 5x + 2 and a line has equation y = −x + k, where k is a constant. (a) Show that the x-coordinates of any points of intersection satisfy x² + 6x + 2 − k = 0. (b) Find the value of k for which the line is a tangent to the curve. (c) Find the set of values of k for which the line meets the curve at two distinct points.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 equates x² + 5x + 2 = −x + k and rearranges [1] (b) M1 (6)² − 4(1)(2 − k) = 0; A1 k = −7 [2] (c) M1 discriminant > 0; A1 k > −7 [2]

items.stem: The discriminant of a quadratic equation is −12. How many real roots does the equation have?
items.markingKey: A negative discriminant means no real roots.

items.stem: Explain why the equation x² + 9 = 0 has no real roots, using the discriminant.
items.answer: a = 1, b = 0, c = 9 so b² − 4ac = −36 < 0, so there are no real roots.
items.markingKey: B1 discriminant −36; B1 negative so no real roots [2]

items.stem: Explain why a quadratic equation cannot have exactly three real roots.
items.answer: A quadratic has at most two roots: the formula gives x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a), which gives at most two values.
items.markingKey: B1 formula gives ± only; B1 at most two values [2]

items.stem: Hana works out the discriminant of 5x² − 4x + 2 = 0 as 16 + 4 × 5 × (2) = 56 and concludes that the equation has two distinct real roots. Explain the error and state the correct conclusion.
items.answer: The discriminant is b² − 4ac, not b² + 4ac: 16 − 4(5)(2) = −24, so the equation has no real roots.
items.markingKey: B1 identifies b² − 4ac; B1 −24 so no real roots

items.stem: Use the discriminant to determine the nature of the roots of x² + 10x − 6 = 0.
items.markingKey: M1 b² − 4ac = 124; A1 two distinct real roots

items.stem: Find the values of k for which the equation 9x² + kx + 16 = 0 has two equal real roots.
Find the set of values of the constant c for which the equation 2x² + 2x + c = 0 has two distinct real roots.
items.markingKey: M1 discriminant 4 − 8c; M1 sets > 0; A1 c < 1/2

items.stem: A curve has equation y = x² − 2x + 10 and a line has equation y = 2x + k, where k is a constant. (a) Find the value of k for which the line is a tangent to the curve. (b) Find the coordinates of the point of contact when the line is a tangent to the curve.

A curve has equation y = x² − 2x − 3 and a line has equation y = 4x + k, where k is a constant. (a) Show that the x-coordinates of any points of intersection satisfy x² − 6x − 3 − k = 0. (b) Find the coordinates of the point of contact when the line is a tangent to the curve. (c) Find the set of values of k for which the line meets the curve at two distinct points. (d) State the number of points of intersection when k = −15.
items.answer: (a) Shown (b) (3, 0) (c) k > −12 (d) 0 (the line does not meet the curve)
items.markingKey: (a) B1 equates x² − 2x − 3 = 4x + k and rearranges [1] (b) M1 x = 3; A1 (3, 0) [2] (c) M1 discriminant > 0; A1 k > −12 [2] (d) B1 0 (discriminant negative since k < −12) [1]

items.stem: Which is the solution of x² > 16?
items.markingKey: Critical values ±4; the curve y = x² − 16 is above the x-axis outside the roots.

items.stem: Explain why the solution of (x − a)(x − b) < 0 with a < b is a single interval, while the solution of (x − a)(x − b) > 0 is two separate intervals.
items.answer: y = (x − a)(x − b) is a U-shaped curve crossing the x-axis at a and b: it is below the axis only between the roots and above it on both sides.
items.markingKey: B1 U-shaped sketch/roots a, b; B1 below between, above outside [2]

items.stem: Explain why it is wrong to solve x² < 4x by dividing both sides by x.
items.answer: x may be negative or zero; dividing by a negative reverses the inequality, so information is lost. Rearrange to x(x − 4) < 0 to get 0 < x < 4.
items.markingKey: B1 sign of x unknown; B1 correct method x(x − 4) < 0 giving 0 < x < 4 [2]

items.stem: Solve the inequality x² − x − 6 ≤ 0.
items.markingKey: M1 factorises (x + 2)(x − 3) or finds critical values −2, 3; A1 −2 ≤ x ≤ 3

items.stem: Solve the inequality 9x² − 3x − 6 ≥ 0.
items.markingKey: M1 factorises or uses formula: critical values −2/3 and 1; A1 both; A1 x ≤ −2/3 or x ≥ 1

items.stem: The curve C has equation y = x² − 14x + 33 and the line L has equation y = −24x + 9. (a) Find the x-coordinates of the points where L meets C. (b) Find the set of values of x for which x² − 14x + 33 ≥ −7.
items.answer: (a) x = −6 and x = −4 (b) x ≤ 4 or x ≥ 10
items.markingKey: (a) M1 equates and rearranges to x² + 10x + 24 = 0; A1 x = −6, −4 [2] (b) M1 (x − 7)² ≥ 9; A1 x ≤ 4 or x ≥ 10 [2]

items.stem: Which inequality is true for all real values of x?
items.markingKey: x² ≥ 0 so x² + 1 ≥ 1 > 0.

items.stem: Explain why x² > 25 cannot be written as x > ±5.
items.answer: x² > 25 holds for x > 5 and also for x < −5 (e.g. x = −6); "x > ±5" would suggest x > −5, which includes 0 where 0² < 25.
items.markingKey: B1 counter-example or both regions; B1 x < −5 or x > 5 [2]

items.stem: Describe how a sketch helps to solve a quadratic inequality such as 2x² − x − 3 ≥ 0.
items.answer: Find the roots (−1 and 3/2), sketch the U-shaped curve through them, and read off where the curve is on or above the x-axis: x ≤ −1 or x ≥ 3/2.
items.markingKey: B1 roots and sketch; B1 reads correct regions with ≥ included [2]

items.stem: Solve the inequality x² − 20x + 91 > 0.
items.markingKey: M1 factorises (x − 7)(x − 13) or finds critical values 7, 13; A1 x < 7 or x > 13

items.stem: Solve the inequality x² − 20x + 75 ≥ 0.
items.markingKey: M1 factorises (x − 5)(x − 15) or finds critical values 5, 15; A1 x ≤ 5 or x ≥ 15

items.stem: Find the set of values of k for which the equation kx² + 6x + k + 8 = 0 has two distinct real roots.
items.markingKey: M1 discriminant 36 − 4k(k + 8); M1 sets > 0 and simplifies to k² + 8k − 9 < 0; M1 critical values −9, 1; A1 −9 < k < 1, k ≠ 0

items.stem: To solve y = x + 1 and x² + y² = 25 simultaneously, the best first step is to
options: substitute x² + y² = 25 into y = x + 1
substitute y = x + 1 into x² + y² = 25
items.answer: substitute y = x + 1 into x² + y² = 25
items.markingKey: Substituting the linear equation into the quadratic gives one equation in x.

items.stem: Explain why, after solving a linear and a quadratic equation simultaneously, each x-value must be substituted into the linear equation to find y.
items.answer: Each x-value gives one point of intersection; using the linear equation gives exactly one matching y for each x, whereas the quadratic may give extra values that are not solutions.
items.markingKey: B1 pairs each x with its own y; B1 linear equation avoids spurious values [2]

items.stem: Explain what it means geometrically if, when solving y = mx + c and y = x² simultaneously, the quadratic in x has no real roots.
items.answer: There are no real solutions, so the line and the curve do not meet.
items.markingKey: B1 no real roots; B1 line does not intersect the curve [2]

items.stem: Solve the simultaneous equations y = 7x − 6 and y = x² − x + 6.
items.markingKey: M1 substitutes to obtain x² − 8x + 12 = 0; M1 solves; A1 x = 2, 6; A1 y = 8, 36

items.stem: Solve the simultaneous equations x − y + 13 = 0 and x² + y² = 85.
items.markingKey: M1 substitutes to obtain x² + 13x + 42 = 0; M1 solves; A1 x = −7, −6; A1 y = 6, 7

items.stem: The line y = −3x + 1 intersects the curve y = x² − 6x + 3 at the points A and B, where A has the smaller x-coordinate. (a) Find the coordinates of the midpoint of AB. (b) Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB, giving your answer in the form ax + by + c = 0.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 FT (3/2, −7/2) [1] (b) B1 gradient 1/3; M1 line through midpoint (3/2, −7/2); A1 x − 3y − 12 = 0 [3]

items.stem: A line and a parabola are solved simultaneously and the resulting quadratic has discriminant 0. The line
options: is a tangent to the parabola
is parallel to the axis of symmetry
items.answer: is a tangent to the parabola
items.markingKey: One repeated solution means exactly one point of contact.

items.stem: Explain why solutions to simultaneous equations should be written as coordinate pairs, such as (2, 5) and (−1, −1).
items.answer: Each solution is a point that satisfies both equations; x = 2 goes only with y = 5, so pairing prevents mixing values.
items.markingKey: B1 each pair satisfies both; B1 values must not be mixed [2]

items.stem: Show that the line y = 4x − 15 is a tangent to the curve y = x² + 10x − 6, and explain how your working shows this.
items.answer: Substitution gives x² + 6x + 9 = 0, i.e. (x + 3)² = 0, which has a repeated root x = −3; a single point of contact means the line is a tangent.
items.markingKey: M1 eliminates y to get x² + 6x + 9 = 0; A1 discriminant 0 / repeated root so tangent at x = −3

items.stem: Solve the simultaneous equations y = x − 2 and y = x² − 4.
Ethan designs a rectangular tile with perimeter 42 cm and area 90 cm². By forming and solving a pair of simultaneous equations, find the length and width of the tile.
items.markingKey: B1 x + y = 21 and xy = 90; M1 substitutes to get x² − 21x + 90 = 0; A1 15 and 6

items.stem: The line y = x − 1 intersects the curve xy = 6 at the points A and B, where A has the smaller x-coordinate. (a) Find the exact length of AB. (b) Find the coordinates of the midpoint of AB.

items.stem: Which substitution turns x⁴ − 13x² + 36 = 0 into a quadratic equation?
items.markingKey: x⁴ = (x²)², so with u = x² the equation is u² − 13u + 36 = 0.

items.stem: Explain why the substitution u = √x can lead to a value of u that must be rejected.
items.answer: √x denotes the non-negative square root, so a negative value of u (e.g. u = −2) gives no value of x.
items.markingKey: B1 √x ≥ 0; B1 negative u rejected [2]

items.stem: Explain why x⁴ − 5x² + 4 = 0 has four real roots but x⁴ + 3x² − 4 = 0 has only two.
items.answer: The first gives x² = 1 or 4, both positive, so x = ±1, ±2. The second gives x² = 1 or −4; x² = −4 has no real solution, leaving x = ±1.
items.markingKey: B1 first: two positive values of x², four roots; B1 second: x² = −4 impossible, two roots [2]

items.stem: Solve the equation x⁴ − 13x² + 36 = 0.
Solve the equation x − 7√x + 6 = 0.
items.markingKey: M1 u = √x: u² − 7u + 6 = 0; A1 u values; A1 x = 1 or x = 36

items.stem: The curve C has equation y = x − 6√x + 5, for x ≥ 0. (a) Write down the coordinates of the point where C meets the y-axis. (b) Find the x-coordinates of the points where C meets the line y = 0.
Answer both parts. (a) Which substitution turns 2x^(2/3) − 5x^(1/3) + 2 = 0 into a quadratic? (b) Which substitution turns x⁴ − 13x² + 36 = 0 into a quadratic equation?
items.markingKey: (a) x^(2/3) = (x^(1/3))². (b) x⁴ = (x²)², so with u = x² the equation is u² − 13u + 36 = 0.

items.stem: Explain why solving an equation in √x by squaring both sides can introduce roots that do not satisfy the original equation.
items.answer: Squaring is not reversible: a = b and a = −b both give a² = b², so solutions of the squared equation must be checked in the original.
items.markingKey: B1 squaring loses the sign; B1 must check solutions [2]

items.stem: Nadia solves x − 2√x − 8 = 0 using u = √x, obtains u = 4 or u = −2, and gives the answer x = 16 or x = 4. Explain the error.
items.answer: √x cannot be negative, so u = −2 must be rejected; checking, x = 4 gives −8 ≠ 0. Only x = 16.
items.markingKey: B1 √x ≥ 0 so u = −2 rejected (or checks x = 4 fails); B1 x = 16 only

items.markingKey: (x − 2)² ≥ 0 so 9 − (x − 2)² ≤ 9, with equality when x = 2.

items.stem: Describe how the vertex of y = (x + p)² + q is related to the graph of y = x².
items.answer: y = (x + p)² + q is y = x² translated by −p in the x-direction and q in the y-direction, so the vertex (0, 0) moves to (−p, q).
items.markingKey: B1 translation by vector (−p, q); B1 vertex (−p, q) [2]

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain why x⁴ − 5x² + 4 = 0 has four real roots but x⁴ + 3x² − 4 = 0 has only two. (b) Explain why solving an equation in √x by squaring both sides can introduce roots that do not satisfy the original equation.
items.answer: (a) The first gives x² = 1 or 4, both positive, so x = ±1, ±2. The second gives x² = 1 or −4; x² = −4 has no real solution, leaving x = ±1. (b) Squaring is not reversible: a = b and a = −b both give a² = b², so solutions of the squared equation must be checked in the original.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 first: two positive values of x², four roots; B1 second: x² = −4 impossible, two roots [2] (b) B1 squaring loses the sign; B1 must check solutions [2]

items.stem: The graph of y = ax² + bx + c lies entirely above the x-axis. Which statement is true?

items.stem: Chloe solves x² + 14x + 48 > 0, finds the critical values −8 and −6, and writes −8 < x < −6. Explain the error, using a sketch of y = x² + 14x + 48, and give the correct solution.
items.answer: The curve is U-shaped, so it is above the x-axis outside the roots; Chloe gave the region where it is negative. Correct: x < −8 or x > −6.

items.stem: The curve C has equation y = x² − 16 and the line L has equation y = 2x − 16. (a) Find the x-coordinates of the points where L meets C. (b) By completing the square, find the least value of y on C. (c) Find the set of values of x for which x² − 16 ≥ −7.
items.answer: (a) x = 0 and x = 2 (b) −16 (c) x ≤ −3 or x ≥ 3
items.markingKey: (a) M1 equates and rearranges to x² − 2x = 0; A1 x = 0, 2 [2] (b) M1 x² − 16; A1 least value −16 [2] (c) M1 x² ≥ 9; A1 x ≤ −3 or x ≥ 3 [2]

items.stem: Elena solves x + y = 2 and x² + y² = 33. Elena writes y = 2 − x and then x² + 4 − x² = 33, so 4 = 33, and concludes there are no solutions. Explain the error and write down the correct quadratic equation in x.
items.answer: (2 − x)² ≠ 4 − x²; it equals x² − 4x + 4. Correct equation: 2x² − 4x − 29 = 0.
items.markingKey: B1 identifies (2 − x)² expanded wrongly; B1 2x² − 4x − 29 = 0 (or simplified equivalent)

items.stem: Kwame solves x + y = 3 and x² + y² = 20. Kwame writes y = 3 − x and then x² + 9 − x² = 20, so 9 = 20, and concludes there are no solutions. Explain the error and write down the correct quadratic equation in x.
items.answer: (3 − x)² ≠ 9 − x²; it equals x² − 6x + 9. Correct equation: 2x² − 6x − 11 = 0.
items.markingKey: B1 identifies (3 − x)² expanded wrongly; B1 2x² − 6x − 11 = 0 (or simplified equivalent)

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Explain why the substitution u = √x can lead to a value of u that must be rejected. (b) Explain why x⁴ − 5x² + 4 = 0 has four real roots but x⁴ + 3x² − 4 = 0 has only two.
items.answer: (a) √x denotes the non-negative square root, so a negative value of u (e.g. u = −2) gives no value of x. (b) The first gives x² = 1 or 4, both positive, so x = ±1, ±2. The second gives x² = 1 or −4; x² = −4 has no real solution, leaving x = ±1.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 √x ≥ 0; B1 negative u rejected [2] (b) B1 first: two positive values of x², four roots; B1 second: x² = −4 impossible, two roots [2]
